correctness.rationale: An interior fixed point would force the open cell to be invariant, so each nonempty color subset is a union of orbits of the permutation. Each nonidentity even permutation has two orbits; an adjacent nonempty disjoint subset rules out using both, and the odd cycle then prevents alternating the two orbits. Thus the action is free. The known RP^3 topology gives the covering by S^3; a free self-map reversing its orientation would have rational Lefschetz number 2, impossible, so the quotient is orientable. Independent reconstruction of the quotient cellular boundaries includes the product-simplex boundary signs and the signs of the even relabeling on each surviving ordered color subset. It recovers ranks (19,46,24) and Smith factors (1^19;1^45,3;1^24). The kernels are primitive sublattices, giving precisely Z/3 in H_1 and zero H_2, with H_0 and H_3 both Z. The central extension E of A4 by C2 has order 24; H_1 gives commutator subgroup of order eight, over V4. A subgroup of order three exists by Cauchy's theorem and acts by a three-cycle on the three nonzero elements of the V4 quotient. If the order-eight group were abelian, the entire commutator would have size at most four, since it is the image of conjugation-minus-identity with the central C2 in its kernel. D8 has a characteristic cyclic subgroup of order four, ruling out the three-cycle. The kernel over V4 is therefore Q8, and the order-three action cycling its cyclic subgroups gives the standard binary tetrahedral semidirect product 2T, isomorphic to SL2(F3). No equivariant round-sphere model is needed.
residual_risks: The chain computation verifies integral homology of this finite ordinary quotient, not the equivariance of any Stiefel model, the fundamental group unaided, or other palettes. The group and cover follow from the separate topological and group-theoretic proof.

value.rationale: The ordinary quotient by even relabelings is a natural way to forget palette labels while retaining orientation of the four-color palette. This determines exact integral torsion and a nonabelian deck group for a distinguished free action on the classical pentagon coloring manifold, in contrast to the rational joint-action invariants and the distinct source quotient. The calculation is exhaustive for that given action, and the type of extension is mathematically meaningful rather than an incidental table count.
